_source: 01 sections 3, 4 and 5: the six attributes, the modifier table, character creation, every derived statistic, and the XP curve. The formulas are written as data so `attributes.js` resolves them and nothing else does arithmetic on a rule.
_attributes: 01 section 3. The abbreviation is the identity the rules are written in ("MIG mod"); the name and the line about what each governs are player-facing, so they live in strings.json.
_range: 01 section 3: scored 3-20, and 18 is the natural maximum at creation.
_modifiers: 01 section 3, the Attribute Modifier Table. Each band is the highest score it covers.
_creation: 01 section 3, Character Creation. Classic rolls in order and may reroll the whole set; Standard rolls six results and assigns them freely.
_derived: 01 section 4. Every formula names the attributes it reads, so the resolver never hard-codes one.

hp._source: Level 1: 10 + VIG score. Each level after: +1d6 + VIG mod (minimum +2).

attack._source: d20 + BA + the attribute the attack uses, plus weapon and skill bonuses.

initiative._source: d6 + AGI mod, rolled each round.

saves._source: d20 + attribute mod + floor(level / 3) vs the effect's DC.

critRange._source: Natural 20, or 19-20 when the LCK mod is +2 or better.

effectDc._source: 01 section 4, Effect DCs. Player abilities use DC 10 + floor(level / 2) + the governing attribute mod; a monster's use DC 10 + floor(HD / 2).

_leveling: 01 section 5. XP to reach level L = 50 x L x (L - 1).

leveling._xpSources: 01 section 5. Each is multiplied by the floor number; monsters carry their own XP in monsters.json.
